findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the EC2 user_data script, which is visible via the instance metadata service and API to anyone with describe-instance permissions, exposing long-lived credentials.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and increasing risk of data exposure if the underlying storage is compromised or snapshots are shared.
The snapshot is created from an unencrypted volume and does not specify encryption, so the snapshot itself remains unencrypted and could expose sensitive data if shared or made public.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management plane of the instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0; combined with public subnet placement and a public IP, this substantially widens the internet-facing attack surface with no compensating controls (e.g., WAF, ALB).
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances in this subnet, increasing exposure of workloads (like web_host) directly to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, unnecessarily increasing network exposure.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block, risking unencrypted storage and potential public exposure of network flow log data.
